text.en:
Currency Act
(CHAPTER 69)
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Coins) (No. 4)
Notification 2011
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 1st January 2012 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

Milled and bearing the words “MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE” and lion symbol.
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2012” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock for all the proof coins.
Inspired by Chinese calligraphy, the dragon in the centre is symbolised by the appropriate Chinese character of the “Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches” to enhance the characteristics of the animal and the oriental cultural flavour. The peony, a traditional Chinese symbol of blessings and festive cheer, incorporated on the body of the dragon, ushers in the Lunar New Year. The 2 Chinese characters signifying the “Year of the Dragon” are at the lower-centre of the design. The denomination of the coin in figures is above the design and the weight in troy oz/grams and fineness of the coin are at the upper circumference for all the coins except for the $2 cupro-nickel coin.
